title: 2023-2027 Strategic Plan and mid-year update
subtitle: Electronic participation for councillors, emergency management by-law, vehicle procurement, encampment staffing, reserves, refugee shelter pressures and Bill 23 uncertainty.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that Council adopt the 2023-2027 Strategic Plan, as amended {{vote:m8}}. The plan sets four integrated priorities: homes for all, climate-aligned growth, equitable services and opportunities, and a resilient organization. Councillors asked staff to tighten wording on the mission statement, the land and car-alternative language, and population figures before it returns to Council.

The committee also received the 2023 Mid-Year Update and recommended amending the 2023 tax-supported capital budget {{vote:m7}}. Staff projected the Region to finish close to budget. Councillors raised encampment-related bylaw staffing, the e-scooter program, airport sustainability and uncertainty about Bill 23 and development charges.

The committee recommended continuing electronic participation for councillors at Council and committee meetings, and directed the Regional Clerk to provide a cost estimate for Council Chamber technology upgrades in the 2024 budget {{vote:m9}}. The consent agenda was also approved {{vote:m1}}. It included the updated Emergency Management By-Law, a Heritage Foundation appointment and pre-budget 2024 vehicle procurement. The committee received the reserves report for information and heard a delegate on affordability and budget scrutiny.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the 2023-2027 Strategic Plan, as amended.
The committee recommended that Council receive the mid-year update and amend the 2023 tax-supported capital budget as set out in Appendix D.

The committee recommended continuing electronic participation for councillors at Council and committee meetings, and directed the Clerk to provide a cost estimate for Council Chamber technology upgrades in the 2024 budget.
As part of the consent agenda, the committee recommended approving the updated Emergency Management By-Law.
As part of the consent agenda, the committee recommended approving pre-budget procurement of vehicles and equipment scheduled for replacement in 2024.
As part of the consent agenda, the committee recommended ratifying an appointment to the Waterloo Regional Heritage Foundation for a term ending June 2026.

debate: On the Strategic Plan, councillors pressed for precision. One asked for a mission phrase about "life's essentials" to be tightened, and others asked to drop "single" from "every single person". Staff said they would refine the wording.

Councillors asked for stronger commitments in the plan, such as "will" instead of "may" on transit and climate measures. They also asked for clearer wording on regional land for affordable housing and on complete streets, and for updated population figures. One councillor said the plan did not address residents' feeling of being unsafe. Another asked how economic growth is covered, and staff said it runs through all four priorities.

On the mid-year update, councillors asked why two bylaw officers were added for encampment work. Staff said encampment duties had crowded out other bylaw work and that the broader approach would return in the 2024 budget. Councillors also noted rising numbers at an encampment site, pressure on shelters from refugee claimants, and a planned request for federal funding.

On Bill 23, staff said parts are not yet proclaimed and regulations are pending, including on land acquisition as a development charge cost. That uncertainty means the projected small surplus could change quickly.

On electronic participation, one councillor wanted costs before approval, and staff said costs would come in the budget process. Councillors supported hybrid access for accessibility and for delegations. Some said in-person attendance should be the norm, and others said hybrid should not be undervalued.

A delegate said cost of living and taxes were a concern and urged scrutiny of operating and capital spending, staffing levels and financial reporting. Councillors asked staff for a brief written response.
